title: Indian Coast Guard CGEPT Recruitment 2026: 365 Vacancies Guide
metaDescription: Indian Coast Guard CGEPT 2026: 365 Navik, Yantrik and Hygienist posts, age limits, eligibility, exam stages and how to apply before the deadline.
headline: Indian Coast Guard CGEPT Recruitment 2026: Apply Now

sections.title: What is the CGEPT recruitment drive?
sections.content:
The Indian Coast Guard, under the Ministry of Defence, opened recruitment for 365 posts through the Coast Guard Enrolled Personnel Test, or CGEPT, for the 01/2027 and 02/2027 batches. The drive covers Navik (General Duty), Navik (Domestic Branch), Yantrik and Hygienist-I posts, and applications were accepted online from 6 October to 21 October 2026 through the official portal.

The Coast Guard guards India's coastline, enforces maritime law, carries out search and rescue at sea and protects the marine environment. Navik (GD) personnel form the backbone of ship crews, Yantriks maintain machinery and electrical systems, and Hygienists support medical care, so the drive offers a genuine seagoing career with a government salary.

sections.title: Eligibility and age limits
sections.content:
For Navik (General Duty), candidates must have passed Class 12 with Mathematics and Physics from a board recognised by the Council of Boards of School Education. Navik (Domestic Branch) requires Class 10, while Yantrik needs Class 10 plus a three or four-year engineering diploma in electrical, mechanical or electronics and telecommunication engineering.

The age limit is generally 18 to 22 years, with post-specific date-of-birth windows: Navik (GD) candidates for the 01/2027 and 02/2027 batches were born between 1 November 2005 and 1 May 2009. Upper age relaxation of three years applies to OBC candidates and five years to SC and ST candidates, as per government rules.

sections.title: Selection stages and exam pattern
sections.content:
Selection runs in stages, starting with a computer-based written test, followed by a physical fitness test, document verification and a medical examination. The written test covers subjects linked to the post, and candidates must clear each stage to move to the next. Zone-wise recruitment applies to Navik (GD) male posts, while other posts are filled on an all-India basis.

Physical standards include running, push-ups and other fitness measures, and the medical examination checks eyesight, hearing and general health to seagoing standards. Candidates should read the official notification carefully before applying, because the exact syllabus, test centres and dates are set out there and can change between batches.

sections.title: Pay, training and career path
sections.content:
Navik personnel start at Pay Level 3, with a basic pay of around 21,700 rupees per month plus allowances such as dearness allowance, sea duty allowance and free rations, which raise the in-hand figure considerably. Yantrik and other trades start at comparable levels, and pay rises with promotion and years of service.

After selection, recruits train at the Coast Guard training establishments before joining ships and shore units. Promotion runs from Navik to Pradhan Navik, Adhikari and beyond, and experienced personnel can move into specialist branches. For young Indians who want a uniformed life at sea, the CGEPT is the main door in.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for Indian Coast Guard Navik GD?
faqs.a: Navik (General Duty) candidates are generally aged 18 to 22 years. For the CGEPT 01/2027 and 02/2027 batches, the date-of-birth window was 1 November 2005 to 1 May 2009. OBC candidates get three years of upper age relaxation and SC and ST candidates get five years, so always confirm the exact window in the official notification for your batch.

faqs.q: What qualification is needed for Navik GD?
faqs.a: Navik (General Duty) requires Class 12 passed with Mathematics and Physics from a board recognised by the Council of Boards of School Education. Navik (Domestic Branch) needs Class 10, and Yantrik needs Class 10 plus a three or four-year AICTE-approved engineering diploma in electrical, mechanical, electronics or telecommunication engineering. Equivalent qualifications are accepted only as the notification allows.

faqs.q: How many vacancies are there in CGEPT 2026?
faqs.a: The 2026 CGEPT drive announced 365 vacancies across Navik (General Duty), Navik (Domestic Branch), Yantrik and Hygienist-I posts for the 01/2027 and 02/2027 batches. Applications opened on 6 October 2026 and closed on 21 October 2026. Vacancy numbers vary by batch and post, so the official notification on the Coast Guard recruitment portal is the only authoritative count.

faqs.q: What is the salary of an Indian Coast Guard Navik?
faqs.a: A Navik starts at Pay Level 3 with a basic pay of around 21,700 rupees per month, plus dearness allowance, sea duty allowance, free rations and other benefits that raise total earnings. Pay grows with promotion to Pradhan Navik and higher ranks, and Coast Guard personnel also receive medical cover, housing support and a pension under government rules.
